title: Compact Ingress Adapter API — brain dump
content:
Purpose and context:

Quick personal notes for a super-light ingress adapter intended for edge/embedded clients that need a compact API surface to talk to Redwood runtime proxies. Goal: minimal wire-state, deterministic handshake, and easy policy expressiveness for client teams that cannot embed full HTTP stacks or want tiny SDKs.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Must be implementable in~ <= 20KB binary SDK (Rust wasi, Go mobile, minimal JS runtime).
- Not a full replacement for our gateway; this is an adapter that normalizes a few common patterns (session, prewarm, limited storage) and forwards to standard Redwood ingress when present.
- Not intended for multi-tenant routing, heavy auth flows, or enterprise SAML flows (those stay on full proxy).
- Compatibility target: TLS+HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2, but API surface assumes a small JSON control channel and optional streaming chunking for responses.

High level flow (happy path):
1) Client starts and constructs an ephemeral session token (E) by POST /v1/adapter/session-init with minimal identity blob.
2) Adapter returns token E and a small routing descriptor (model_hint, ttl_seconds, preferred_batch_key).
3) For inference, client POSTs to /v1/adapter/infer with E, payload (prompt or embedding request), and optional call metadata (latency deadline, cost-bound).
4) Adapter applies tenant-local policy (prefilters: sanitize, redact), canonicalizes the request shape, attaches trace headers, and forwards to Redwood ingress endpoint (hosted or dedicated) signed with service-level credentials.
5) Response returned as either: immediate JSON or streaming newline-delimited chunks. Adapter does minimal transform and returns to client.

Minimal API shapes (compact JSON examples) — these are intentionally tiny keys:

Session init request:
{
  "i":"client-id-or-empty",
  "m":"model_hint|gpt-4x-small",
  "p":{"cap":"local-cache:64","q":"fast"}  // policy hints
}

Session init response:
{
  "t":"Epc_abc123",
  "r":"us-west-2:hosted-v2",
  "ttl":3600
}

Inference request (non-stream):
{
  "t":"Epc_abc123",
  "q":"Summarize: the call graph is...",
  "k":"chat",
  "d":5000  // deadline ms (client-side deadline in ms)
}

Inference streaming chunk (server->client) NDJSON lines:
{"c":"partial text chunk 1"}
{"c":"more text"}
{"e":true}  // end flag optional

Design notes for compactness:
- Use 1- or 2-letter keys (i,t,r,q,k,d,c,e) to reduce payload and simplify parsers.
- Keep session token opaque; adapter stores mapping to longer backend auth.
- Model hints (m) are advisory only; backend makes final selection.
- Policy hint "p" lets client request local cache, quant preference etc. Adapter uses it to pick fast-path or remote fallback.

Headers and auth:
- Client->adapter uses TLS and a short-lived client cert or pre-shared key in header X-A-PSK: base64.
- Adapter authenticates to Redwood using a long-lived service credential; client never learns service creds.
- Trace headers: X-Trace: <hex> forwarded.

Local caching and offline support (opinionated):
- Adapter should implement a tiny LRU prefix cache for KV (small prompt textiles), with TTLs set by backend route hints.
- When offline, adapter accepts inference requests and returns a 202 with body {"r":"queued","id":"uuid"} then replays when online — best-effort only.
- Important: offline semantics must include staleness label on eventual responses (header or chunk field "s":"stale" or "fresh").

Routing descriptor (returned on session-init):
- r: host hint (string)
- preferred_batch_key: a short token to co-locate similar requests on same pool (improves batching)
- fallback_tier: e.g., "cpu-fast" or "quant-small"

Server-side forwarding (adapter->redwood): canonicalized minimal envelope: 
{
  "source":"adapter",
  "st":"Epc_abc123",
  "payload":{...}  // full Redwood request forwarded
}

ASCII sequence diagram (very rough):

Client  Adapter     Redwood
  |       |            |
  |--init->|            |
  |       |--auth->     |
  |       |<--token-----|
  |<-t-----|            |
  |--infer->|--forward->|
  |       |<--resp-------|
  |<-chunk--|            |

Decision log / tradeoffs:
- Compact keys reduce bandwidth but make debugging harder. Decide: provide optional "pretty" mode (full keys) toggled by header X-Adapter-Mode: pretty.
- Session TTL and revocation: sessions are short-lived (1hr default). For long-running clients we rotate token via silent refresh endpoint /v1/adapter/session-refresh.
- Streaming: use NDJSON for very small client parsers; consider optional length-prefixed binary for wasm later.

Open questions:
- Do we need a feature negotiation step (capabilities) on init? probably yes to allow server to avoid sending chunks if client cannot parse streaming. Add boolean in init request "c":"capabilities-bitmask".
- How much policy expressiveness do we allow via "p" hint? risk of client gaming cost. Maybe restrict to whitelisted options per org.
- Should we include a signer for payload integrity from client? Adds complexity; skip for v1.

TODO (next actions):
- Get Miguel to sketch tiny Rust wasm client for session-init + streaming decode (low effort).
- Add unit test vectors for NDJSON chunk parsing and stale flag.
- Draft a short internal Confluence page with examples and debugging cheats.
- Prototype adapter runtime that maps compact envelope -> Redwood full envelope (PR template referenced above).

Misc notes / random thoughts:
- Might be handy to support a small "route hint" that embeds a cost cap (e.g., max_tokens: 128, max_cost_cents: 2) — cheap clients will benefit.
- For observability, adapter should emit only per-session sampled traces (1% default) to avoid telemetry explosion. Trace id propagation must be preserved across forward.
- Consider a companion CLI (tiny) that replicates the compact shapes for dev testing (like curl but tiny).

End of brain dump — this is rough; goals are: tiny client SDK, deterministic handshake, minimal server-side transform, and explicit escape hatches (pretty mode, capability flags).

If this lands well we can fold into the proxy-adapters repo and add an experimental tag in the registry.
